about: Test vectors for Trigon's package-URL canonicalisation, version 1. Every writer and reader of the purl1 and pkg1 lookup keys (docs/19-distribution-and-lookup.md section 5) must produce `canonical` and `package` exactly from `input`, and refuse every entry of `invalid`. `canonical` is what a statement signs as `purl` and what the purl1 key hashes; `package` is the package with nothing that names one version of it, what the pkg1 key hashes: pkg:<type>/<namespace>/<name>, plus the repository_url qualifier where there is one, and no version, no subpath and no other qualifier. The rules are in crates/trigon-core/src/purl.rs and docs/09-attestations.md.

vectors.why: already canonical
the scheme is case-insensitive
slashes after the scheme are ignored, as the purl spec requires of a parser
the type is lowercased
an npm name is lowercased
an npm scope is a namespace, and its @ is encoded
an unencoded scope: an @ that begins a path segment is never the version separator
no version: the scope's @ is still not a separator
the purl spec lowercases an npm name and says nothing of the namespace
an escape of an unreserved character is decoded
PEP 503: lowercase, and each run of - _ . is one -
PEP 503 maps . as well as _, where the purl spec maps only _
a run of separators is one -
a qualifier that names one version's file is not in the versionless form, which finds every version
github lowercases namespace and name; the version keeps its case
bitbucket lowercases namespace and name
composer lowercases namespace and name
deb lowercases namespace and name; a colon is never encoded; the versionless form keeps no qualifier but repository_url
rpm lowercases the namespace and keeps the name's case; arch is not part of the package
hex lowercases the name
the purl spec gives nuget no case rule, so the name keeps its case
qualifier keys are lowercased and sorted; maven keeps its case; the versionless form drops them
a slash in a qualifier value is not encoded; repository_url stays in the versionless form, because the same name on another registry is another package
empty namespace segments and a trailing slash are dropped
golang keeps its case; subpath segments that are empty, . or .. are dropped; the versionless form has no subpath
a subpath segment is dropped by what it decodes to: %2E%2E is .., which is dropped, and not written back out as ..
encoded . and .. segments are dropped whatever the case of their hex
a subpath that is only an encoded . is no subpath
an encoded slash is part of one segment and never splits it, so a%2F.. is one segment and not a ..
an encoded colon is decoded; repository_url stays in the versionless form
a + is encoded, with uppercase hex
lowercase hex in an escape becomes uppercase
crates.io, which Trigon accepts as a type, is cargo
rubygems, which Trigon accepts as a type, is gem
qualifiers are sorted, and a colon or a slash in a qualifier value is written as itself; download_url and checksum name one version's file, so the versionless form has neither
@ ? # & and = stay encoded wherever they would be read as separators
non-ASCII is UTF-8, percent-encoded, whether it arrived raw or encoded
lowercasing is of ASCII letters only: KELVIN SIGN (U+212A) stays itself, and never becomes the k of keras
PEP 503's lowercasing is of ASCII letters too, so this is not pkg:pypi/keras
U+0130 keeps its case, since full and simple case mapping lowercase it differently; the ASCII letters after it are lowercased
a namespace is lowercased in ASCII only as well: A-diaeresis (U+00C4) keeps its case
a qualifier with an empty value is dropped, and so are empty pairs
an empty qualifier string is no qualifiers
an empty subpath is no subpath
the versionless form keeps repository_url, encoded as any qualifier value is, and drops the version, the subpath and every other qualifier
two versions that name their own files share one versionless key, which is what finds every version

invalid.why: the @ begins the last segment, so it is the version separator, and there is no name before it
a type does not start with a digit
a version separator with no version
an escape needs two hex digits
a trailing % is not an escape
a sign is not a hex digit
decodes to bytes that are not UTF-8
a qualifier key given twice, compared lowercased
a qualifier key given twice, even where one value is empty
a qualifier key does not start with a digit
a qualifier key is never percent-encoded
whitespace inside a component: encode it as %20
